This documentary series focuses on the rich history and fascinating tales surrounding gold mining trails and abandoned ghost towns. Created and produced by Kelowna-based television station CHBC-TV, it features host Mike Roberts along with historian storyteller Bill Barlee.

Filmed within a studio reminiscent of an old trapper’s cabin, the program delves into the early 20th-century gold rush era in British Columbia. Through interviews and discussions with historians, they explore the stories behind some of the most significant gold discoveries and the impact these events had on local communities and economies.

In the early days of comics, before the Silver Age of Comic Books arrived, there were some exciting stories. One of these was "Strange Adventures," a series that came out of DC Comics. This comic had its first issue on September 1950, making it the very first science fiction comic book ever made.

The first issue introduced us to something called "Destination Moon," which inspired the plot of another famous comic called "Strange Adventures." In the eighth issue of this comic, we got a special surprise! An illustration of a monkey wearing glasses caught people's eyes. This wasn't just any monkey; it was actually a superhero named Captain Comet!

John Broome, who wrote many popular comic books at the time, helped create Captain Comet. He imagined a brave astronaut who could fly like a bird and fight bad guys. His idea became so popular that other artists started drawing Captain Comet too. Over time, he became one of the last heroes of the pre-Silver Age era, which means his adventures ended when the Silver Age started.

So, "Strange Adventures" not only brought us exciting space stories but also gave us a glimpse into the world of Captain Comet, the first superhero to wear a red cape and blue helmet, known as the "Red Tornado."
